A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, continuous-time framework, theoretical results, and toy simulations. All 26 pages of v2 and 41 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: Appendix A.2 reports original initialization, switched-system forgetting, and tracking simulations, including Figures 1–2 and Table 1.

after.justification: Appendix B retains those simulations. Section 8 and Appendix C additionally report original SST/Mamba forecasting experiments, ablations, and perturbation evaluations.

M1.justification: Beyond v2's continuous-time LMI penalty for a two-state toy SSM, v3 introduces a sampled block-LMI penalty for the discrete Mamba selective-scan recurrence and integrates it into SST training (Section 6). Implemented variants include learnable diagonal storage and an additional router-energy penalty. The original toy procedure remains in Appendix B.3.

E1.justification: v3 retains the synthetic studies and adds forecasting on ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, weather, electricity, and traffic. It also evaluates corrupted-input scenarios using Gaussian noise, spikes, block masks, amplitude shifts, and last-value-hold (Section 8).

E2.justification: The original toy comparators remain. v3 adds unregularized SST and projection-only SST controls, alongside comparisons involving identity versus diagonal storage, projection variants, and router regularization (Tables 3–6 and 8; Appendix C.4). These expand the evaluated comparator set beyond v2's toy-model comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds a forecasting protocol with standard train/validation/test splits, four horizons of 96/192/336/720, a 672-token look-back window, and label length 336. New evaluations measure MSE, MAE, sampled LMI violations, state norms, and router behavior; corruption tests alter inputs while retaining clean targets. The retained toy protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of identity versus learnable diagonal storage, regularization strength, PSD projection, router-energy penalties, and five input perturbations. Sections 8.3–8.5 and Appendix C investigate conservativeness, sensitivity, internal robustness, and whether routing becomes energy-aware. The earlier initialization and forgetting studies remain.

E5.justification: v2 does not specify repeated-run or seed reporting. Appendix C.1 now states three training seeds per SST variant and averaging over seeds; Section 8.4 also specifies three-seed perturbation evaluation. No confidence intervals, run-to-run error bars, or specified significance tests accompany these results. This does not establish additional runs of the retained toy studies.

E6.justification: The toy results are unchanged, including v2 Table 1 becoming v3 Table 7. Newly added SST results report baseline versus regularized mean LMI violations of 0.035824 versus 0.002882 and clean MSE of 0.385804 versus 0.385815 (Table 3). Table 5 reports nearly identical robust MSE, 0.70808 versus 0.70809, alongside improved internal diagnostics. These are new experiments, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The continuous-time theorems and appendix proofs are retained, including ISS Theorem 6.1 becoming Theorem 7.1. v3 adds discrete selective-scan dynamics, a one-step dissipativity definition, and Proposition 6.1 deriving the sampled block LMI with a proof sketch. Discrete rank-monotonicity and irreversibility proofs remain future work.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the main continuous-time claims but add a practical contribution: a differentiable discrete Mamba-core regularizer supported by real forecasting experiments. New headline claims concern reduced sampled violations with little clean-MSE change and improved internal diagnostics under corruption, explicitly without claiming improved robust forecasting MSE.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes soft Mamba-core diagnostics from certified passivity and full-network robustness, and adds explanations for absent robust-MSE gains and ineffective energy-aware routing (Sections 8.4–8.6). It reframes the retained simulations as pedagogical toy studies and revises future directions toward network-level guarantees, perturbation-aware training, and remaining discrete-time theory.

D1.justification: Sections 6.3 and C.1 add per-token matrix extraction and eigendecomposition details, SST dimensions and head counts, sequence settings, storage initialization, and regularization parameters. Appendix C also states that aggregate analysis CSVs and plots are released. Reproducibility remains incomplete: optimizer, schedule, and epoch details are deferred to SST defaults, and perturbation strengths are unspecified.

R1.justification: New Table 1 and revised related work explicitly separate classical LTV/ISS ingredients from selective-SSM specialization and the practical Mamba regularizer. A sampled-data subsection is added, and positioning relative to Lyapunov-exponent analyses is revised around training-time intervention. New references include Xu et al. (2025) on SST and Zubić et al. (2026) on multilayer SSM expressivity.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, preliminaries, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. v3 adds intuitive explanations and theorem-specific ML implications, inserts dedicated discrete-method and empirical sections, and reorganizes the appendix into proofs, retained toy simulations, and extended forecasting experiments.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation with contribution and notation tables plus benchmark, ablation, and robustness displays. The original Figures 1–2 become Figures 3–4, and Table 1 becomes Table 7. New caption/display mismatches occur: Figure 2 shows perturbation-mode bars rather than the described Pareto plot, while Figure 5 shows dataset-level MSE rather than the described per-run deltas.

improvement.justification: v3 partially addresses v2's explicit discrete-time implementation gap through a sampled Mamba-core criterion and real forecasting experiments, while more carefully limiting practical robustness claims. These improve applicability and claim calibration. The net gain is tempered by mismatched figures and captions, especially Figures 2 and 5, and incomplete protocol and uncertainty reporting, which weaken readers' ability to verify the finer empirical claims.
